title: Allegedly: sources and reported claims in the news
title_target: Ska ha? Då vet de alltså inte säkert.
goal: Read a Swedish news article critically: tell a fact from a reported claim, and hear how far the journalist vouches for what they pass on.
bekal: you can use and understand *ska ha* + supine: “is said to have done”
you can rank reporting verbs from neutral (*säger*, *uppger*) to distancing (*hävdar*, *påstår*)
you can read the parts of a news article and apply the four classic questions of *källkritik*
wave: Go back to Unit 6: find three s-passive headlines on a Swedish news site (such as *Man greps i natt* or *Skolan stängs*) and rewrite each one in the active with *man* or a named subject.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Lördagsfrukost
dialogs.intro: Saturday morning in the flat on Södermalm. Dian's thesis has been handed in, and she is reading the news on her phone over breakfast. Elin, who teaches source criticism to school classes at her library, looks over her shoulder.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Har du sett det här? ”Byggbolag ska ha fuskat med miljömärkning.”
lines.id: Have you seen this? “Construction company allegedly cheated on eco-labeling.”
lines.literal: have you seen this here? “building-company shall have cheated with environment-labeling.”

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: ”Ska ha”? Då vet de alltså inte säkert.
lines.id: “Allegedly”? So they don't know for sure.
lines.literal: “shall have”? then know they thus not surely.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Nej, det är uppgifter som tidningen har fått. Ingen har bekräftat dem än.
lines.id: No, it's information the paper has been given. Nobody has confirmed it yet.
lines.literal: no, it is informations that newspaper-the has got. nobody has confirmed them yet.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Och vem uppger det? Står det någon källa?
lines.id: And who's saying so? Does it name a source?
lines.literal: and who states it? stands it any source?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: ”Enligt uppgifter till Stadsbladet” – alltså anonyma källor inom bolaget.
lines.id: “According to information obtained by Stadsbladet” — so, anonymous sources inside the company.
lines.literal: “according-to informations to Stadsbladet” — thus anonymous sources within company-the.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Då ska man vara lite försiktig. Vad säger bolaget själv?
lines.id: Then you should be a little careful. What does the company itself say?
lines.literal: then shall one be little careful. what says company-the self?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Presschefen tillbakavisar alltihop. Hon hävdar att de har följt alla regler.
lines.id: The press officer rejects all of it. She claims they've followed every rule.
lines.literal: press-chief-the back-rejects all-of-it. she claims that they have followed all rules.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Lägg märke till ordet ”hävdar”. Där tar journalisten lite avstånd.
lines.id: Notice the word “claims”. That's where the journalist keeps a little distance.
lines.literal: lay mark to word-the “claims”. there takes journalist-the little distance.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och ”säger” är helt neutralt?
lines.id: And “says” is completely neutral?
lines.literal: and “says” is wholly neutral?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Precis. ”Uppger” är också neutralt, bara lite torrare. Det är nyheternas favoritord.
lines.id: Exactly. “Uppger” is neutral too, just a bit drier. It's the news's favorite word.
lines.literal: exactly. “states” is also neutral, only little drier. it is news-the's favorite-word.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Synd att uppsatsen redan är inlämnad. Det här hade varit ett perfekt exempel.
lines.id: Shame my thesis is already handed in. This would have been a perfect example.
lines.literal: pity that essay-the already is handed-in. this here had been a perfect example.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Spara det till nästa gång. Men kolla primärkällan först – det lär jag ut till varenda skolklass.
lines.id: Save it for next time. But check the primary source first — I teach that to every single school class.
lines.literal: save it to next time. but check primary-source-the first — that learn I out to every-single school-class.

notes: **Ska ha fuskat** — *ska* + *ha* + supine means “is said to have cheated, allegedly cheated”. This *ska* has nothing to do with the future: it is the reporting *ska*, and it tells you the writer is passing on a claim without vouching for it. Elin's instant echo — *”Ska ha”?* — shows how clearly a native speaker hears that signal.

**Uppgifter** — you met *en uppgift* (**ÜP-yift**) as “a task, an assignment”. In the news, the plural almost always means “information, reports, claims”: *enligt uppgifter* = “according to reports”, *uppgifterna stämmer* = “the reports are accurate”, *uppgifterna tillbakavisas* = “the claims are rejected”.

**Står det någon källa?** — *det står* is how Swedish says what a text “says”: *Det står i tidningen att…* = “It says in the paper that…”. **Källa** (**SHEL-lah**) means both “spring, well” and “source”; *k* before *ä* is soft, as in *kär* and *kök*.

**Tillbakavisar** (**til-BAH-kah-vee-sar**) — “rejects, dismisses”, used only for claims and accusations. It is formal; in conversation people say *säger att det inte stämmer*. Notice *alltihop* (“all of it, the whole lot”), the spoken version of *allting*.
**Lägg märke till** — “notice, pay attention to”, literally “lay a mark to”. The related adjective *märkbar* (“noticeable”) follows the word-formation pattern from Unit 10.

**Lär ut** — *lära ut* is “to teach (something to others)”, while *lära sig* is “to learn”. Swedish libraries take an active role in teaching *källkritik* (source criticism) to schoolchildren, so for Elin this really is part of the job.

grammars.title: The reporting ska: “is said to (have)”
body: Swedish has a compact way to pass on what others claim, where English needs *allegedly*, *reportedly* or *is said to*. It is so common in headlines that you need to recognize it instantly.

head: Form
Meaning
Example
rows: Restaurangen **ska vara** jättebra. — The restaurant is supposed to be really good.
Ministern **ska ha sagt** att skatten höjs. — The minister reportedly said taxes are going up.
Han **ska inte ha vetat** om felet. — He reportedly didn't know about the error.
Hon **lär ha flyttat** till Umeå. — Apparently she's moved to Umeå.
Huset **sägs ha byggts** på 1700-talet. — The house is said to have been built in the 1700s.

after: How do you tell reporting *ska* from future *ska*? Look at what follows. *Han ska åka* is a plan (“he's going to leave”); *Han ska ha åkt* is a report (“he's said to have left”). With *vara*, context decides: *Filmen ska vara bra* almost always means “is supposed to be good”, not “will be good”.
*Lär* (Unit 4) is close, but it sounds more like hearsay among friends; *ska ha* is the journalist's tool. Neither of them is used by someone who knows the fact first-hand.

grammars.title: Reporting verbs: how far does the writer vouch?
body: Swedish journalists choose their reporting verb with care, and readers notice. Learn the verbs as a scale.

head: Verb
Say it
Past · Supine
What it signals
rows: claims; the writer keeps a distance

after: *Uppge*, *medge* and *påstå* are built on the strong verbs *ge* and *stå*, so they inflect like them: *gav · gett*, *stod · stått*. The supines *uppgivit* and *medgivit* also exist and are common in writing.
In everyday conversation *påstå* is often an accusation in itself: *Påstår du att jag ljuger?* — “Are you saying I'm lying?”

dialogs.title: Text — Nyhetsartikeln
dialogs.intro: Here is the article Dian was reading, as it appeared in the (fictional) Stockholm daily Stadsbladet. Read it twice: once for the facts, once for the verbs that tell you who is saying what.

lines.speaker: Rubrik:
lines.text: Byggbolag ska ha fuskat med miljömärkning
lines.id: Construction company allegedly cheated on eco-labeling
lines.literal: building-company shall have cheated with environment-labeling

lines.speaker: Ingress:
lines.text: Ett av Stockholms största byggbolag ska ha fuskat med miljömärkningen av flera nya bostadshus. Det uppger anonyma källor inom företaget för Stadsbladet.
lines.id: One of Stockholm's largest construction companies is alleged to have cheated on the eco-labeling of several new apartment buildings, anonymous sources inside the company have told Stadsbladet.
lines.literal: …it states anonymous sources within company-the for Stadsbladet.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Enligt uppgifterna ska energiförbrukningen i husen vara upp till 40 procent högre än vad som anges i certifikaten.
lines.id: According to the reports, energy consumption in the buildings is up to 40 percent higher than stated in the certificates.
lines.literal: according-to informations-the shall energy-consumption-the in houses-the be up to 40 percent higher than what that is-stated in certificates-the.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Bolagets presschef Maria Lind tillbakavisar uppgifterna.
lines.id: The company's press officer, Maria Lind, rejects the claims.
lines.literal: company-the's press-chief Maria Lind back-rejects informations-the.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: – Vi har följt alla regler. Certifieringen har gjorts av en oberoende part, säger hon till Stadsbladet.
lines.id: “We've followed every rule. The certification was carried out by an independent party,” she tells Stadsbladet.
lines.literal: — we have followed all rules. certification-the has been-done by an independent party, says she to Stadsbladet.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Flera boende hävdar dock att de har klagat på höga elräkningar i över ett år.
lines.id: Several residents, however, claim they have been complaining about high electricity bills for over a year.
lines.literal: several residing claim however that they have complained on high electricity-bills in over a year.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: – Vi fick höra att det var barnsjukdomar, säger en av dem, som vill vara anonym.
lines.id: “We were told it was teething problems,” says one of them, who wishes to remain anonymous.
lines.literal: — we got hear that it was child-diseases, says one of them, who wants be anonymous.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Kommunen uppges nu granska samtliga bygglov som bolaget har fått sedan 2022.
lines.id: The city is now reported to be reviewing every building permit the company has received since 2022.
lines.literal: municipality-the is-stated now examine all building-permits that company-the has got since 2022.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Enligt en expert som Stadsbladet har talat med kan bolaget få svårt att vinna nya upphandlingar om uppgifterna stämmer.
lines.id: According to an expert Stadsbladet has spoken to, the company may find it hard to win new public contracts if the reports are true.
lines.literal: according-to an expert that Stadsbladet has talked with can company-the get hard to win new procurements if informations-the tally.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Stadsbladet har sökt ansvarigt kommunalråd, som ännu inte har återkommit.
lines.id: Stadsbladet has tried to reach the city commissioner responsible, who has not yet responded.
lines.literal: Stadsbladet has sought responsible municipal-councillor, who yet not has come-back.

notes: **Rubrik** and **ingress** — the headline and the lead paragraph. Headlines drop articles (*Byggbolag*, not *Ett byggbolag*) and love the reporting *ska ha*. The *ingress*, usually in bold, packs the whole story into one or two sentences.

**Det uppger anonyma källor … för Stadsbladet** — the standard way to close an *ingress*. *Det* points back to the whole previous sentence and takes first place, so the verb comes second and the source only after it. English puts the source in a tag at the end (“…, sources told Stadsbladet”); Swedish gives it its own sentence. Note *uppge för* + the outlet: “state to”.

**– Vi har följt alla regler.** Swedish journalism marks direct speech with a dash (*talstreck*) at the start of the line, not with quotation marks. The speaker tag follows with inversion: *…, **säger hon** till Stadsbladet.*

**Dock** (**dok**) — “however”, the written word for *men* or *däremot*. It nearly always sits after the verb, in the middle of the sentence: *Flera boende hävdar **dock**…*. And notice *boende* — a present participle used as a noun, “residents, people living there”.
**Barnsjukdomar** — literally “childhood diseases”, figuratively “teething problems” in a new product or building. Swedish chose the illness, English chose the teeth.

**Har sökt ansvarigt kommunalråd** — *söka någon* means “try to reach someone”, and this sentence is a fixed formula at the end of Swedish news stories. In this telegraphic style the noun drops its article: *ansvarig minister*, *ansvarigt kommunalråd* (*ett kommunalråd*, so *-t*).

grammars.title: News passives: uppges, sägs, väntas, beräknas
body: A handful of s-passive verbs followed by an infinitive let a journalist report something without naming who said it. They work like English “is reported to”, “is expected to”.
after: These verbs combine with *ha* + supine for the past, just like *ska*: *Bolaget **uppges ha** fuskat* = “The company is reported to have cheated.” The two forms *ska ha fuskat* and *uppges ha fuskat* are near-synonyms; *uppges* sounds slightly more official.

**Enligt** (“according to”) is the third tool: *enligt uppgifterna*, *enligt polisen*, *enligt en expert som Stadsbladet har talat med*. It always opens an adverbial, so if it comes first, the verb follows directly: *Enligt uppgifterna **ska** energiförbrukningen…*

sections.title: Anatomy of a Swedish news article

head: Part
Swedish
What to expect
rows: no articles, present tense, *ska ha* for claims
who, what, where in 1–2 sentences; source at the end with *Det uppger…*
introduced by a dash, tag with inversion: *säger hon*
a word or two breaking up a long article
the other side's answer, or *har inte återkommit*

blocks.text: Swedish news is written according to the same ideal as Swedish discussion (Unit 11): *sakligt*. Opinion is labeled as such — look for the words **ledare** (editorial), **krönika** (column), **debatt** or **kultur** at the top of the page. A **nyhetsartikel** with opinion in it would break the rules, and readers complain.

blocks.title: Hearing the distance
items: *Polisen **bekräftar** att en man har gripits.* — fact, confirmed.
*Mannen **uppges** vara i 40-årsåldern.* — reported, not yet confirmed.
*Mannen **ska ha** hotat personalen.* — claim passed on.
*Mannen **påstår** att han var hemma.* — the writer is visibly skeptical.

blocks.text: Swedish schoolchildren learn **källkritik** (**SHEL-kri-teek**), source criticism, from an early age, and it is built on four criteria with short Swedish names. They are as useful for a TikTok clip as for a historical document.

head: Criterion
Say it
The question
Applied to the article
rows: Is the source what it claims to be?
Is Stadsbladet a real newspaper with a responsible editor?
How close in time to the events is it?
When were the complaints made, and when was this written?
Is it first-hand, or copied from someone else?
The residents are first-hand; the anonymous sources are unknown.
Does the source have a reason to bend the truth?
The press officer is paid to defend the company.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 4
items: Unit 4 taught you to hedge your own claims: *lär*, *torde*, *verkar*, *tycks*, *förmodligen*.
This unit is the mirror image: hedging what *others* claim. Say the same fact in three ways: *Bolaget har fuskat.* · *Bolaget verkar ha fuskat.* · *Bolaget ska ha fuskat.*
Which one would get a journalist sued if it turned out to be false? (The first.)

vocab.en: a report, a piece of information (in the news)
a city/municipal commissioner (a full-time local politician)

answers: ska ha — ska — ha — uppges — väntas
Han ska ha sagt det. — Presschefen tillbakavisar uppgifterna. — Det uppger anonyma källor för Stadsbladet. — Enligt uppgifterna ska bolaget ha fuskat.

Bolaget ska ha fuskat med certifikaten. — Kommunalrådet ska ha vetat om problemet. — Presschefen ska ha ljugit för journalisten. — Husen ska ha förbrukat mer energi än utlovat. — Ingen ska ha kontrollerat siffrorna.
Enligt tidningen ska bolaget ha fuskat. — Ministern förnekar allting. — Flera boende hävdar att de har klagat. — Kolla primärkällan först. — Beslutet väntas nästa vecka.
